To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the environmental performance of plastic recycling facilities in highly urbanized regions such that Singapore is highly sensitive to the transport distances traveled, and the type of truck used to transport the plastic waste.

The life cycle greenhouse gas emission of small-scale distributed plastic recycling compared with large-scale centralized systems is sensitive to the transport distances travelled and type of trucks used.

the life cycle environmental impact of small-scale distributed plastic recycling systems compared to large-scale centralized systems depends on the distance of transport and the type of vehicles used.

the environmental performance of small scale distributed systems is highly sensitive to the transport distances traveled and the type and capacity of the trucks used.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the environmental impact of plastic waste recycling can be reduced by increasing the amount of recycling, but this is not always possible in urbanized settings due to the limited amount of available space.

we developed a model that simulates a plastic sorting and recycling facility network in Singapore, and used it to evaluate the environmental performance of different facility configurations and scenarios.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the life cycle assessment results for the distributed recycling scenario are sensitive to the assumptions made regarding the transport distance traveled.
the environmental performance of plastic recycling systems is dependent on the type of plastic waste stream, the type of plastic material, and the scale of the system.
distributed recycling facilities can be more environmentally friendly than large-scale centralized facilities if the transportation distances are minimized and the right type of trucks are used.
